answer: Each identity smelts one ore lot in a tundra forge and posts a signed slag record: ore mass, slag mass, lot number. A sparrow auditor recomputes slag from the tundra assay table and burns the 70-credit bond on slag over 2% off or a repeated lot number. The first lot costs 37 credits; the k-th costs 37+7(k-1), since each lot needs its own ore, slot, assay. The 1000th lot costs 7030, so 1000 fakes cost 3,533,500 plus 70,000 bonds; an honest agent pays once and redeems its bond. A rented-slag ring fails: bought slag carries another lot's balance, and recomputation against the lot exposes it.
